key_insight: The paper generates valid correlation matrices on graph-defined sparsity patterns by projecting an initial matrix onto the elliptope with convex optimization, while optionally controlling the off-diagonal mean.
engineering_relevance: This provides a tunable way to synthesize realistic benchmark correlation data for testing graphical model inference, especially when matrix structure and sparsity must match a known network.
method: Set absent edges to zero and diagonal entries to one, then solve a convex projection onto the positive semidefinite elliptope.
Use numerical schemes to compute feasible correlation matrices under graph constraints.
Optionally impose a target mean on off-diagonal entries to better match realistic data distributions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation studies plus applications to neuroscience and finance datasets, and compares the approach with GAN-based correlation matrix generation.
watch_item: The method is not intended to sample uniformly from the feasible set, so generated matrices are principled but may be biased toward the chosen projection and mean settings.
paper_title: Graph-Based Correlation Matrix Generation: A Convex Optimization Approach
